name: Stalinism
summary: Stalinism is the system of rule built in the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin from the late 1920s to 1953. It combined socialism in one country, a planned state-owned economy, forced collectivization and rapid industrialization with a one-party state, a personality cult and mass repression justified by an intensifying class struggle. Its adherents present it as Marxism-Leninism.
scope: The Soviet system of 1927-1953 as set out in Stalin's own works (the 1939 Report to the 18th Party Congress, Dizzy with Success, Economic Problems of Socialism in the USSR) and described in the scholarship. It excludes Trotskyism, Maoism, Hoxhaism and post-1956 de-Stalinised Marxism-Leninism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: State socialism puts health services under state provision and planning, so a free universal system follows from its principles.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set by the state plan rather than by a legal minimum, so the question barely applies; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Stalin kept only limited commodity exchange for consumer goods and held that planning, not competition, directs production.

public-ownership.rationale: Industry is state property, which Stalin treats as the foundation of socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No private wealthy class is meant to survive; inferred from dispossession of exploiter classes.

unions-good.rationale: Unions exist but as party-led bodies serving the plan; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production was abolished and kulaks dispossessed; only personal property is protected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: There are no private corporations; where private activity remains it is under state control; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The state is meant to provide for workers, though work is expected of all; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is vested in the state or in collective farms as a whole, not in each enterprise's workforce.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Stalin held that a socialist state needs a strong intelligence service and punitive organs; the NKVD ran mass surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A tightly policed state is unlikely to permit it; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The state controlled speech broadly and officially condemned racial chauvinism; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The system centred on one leader and a cult of personality from 1929 to 1953 (s1); this is documented practice rather than a stated doctrine of bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Stalin argued the state must grow stronger, not wither, under capitalist encirclement.

limit-guns.rationale: The state held a monopoly on arms; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Stalin stressed a strong army, punitive organs and intelligence service; the security apparatus grew enormously.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prostitution was treated as a capitalist vestige; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Power was centralised in the party and the planning state (s1), so decisions belong to the centre rather than local bodies.

rehabilitation.rationale: Punishment was harsh, with mass executions and camps, though labour 'correction' was the official language.

traditional-family.rationale: The regime reversed Lenin-era family liberalisation, banning abortion in 1936 and re-criminalising homosexuality in 1934.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexuality was re-criminalised in 1934 (s1), so same-sex marriage is firmly rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion was banned again in 1936 (s1), reversing the earlier legalisation.

more-religion-public.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and mass persecution of religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Official doctrine condemned racism and promoted the friendship of peoples; inferred, though practice included ethnic deportations.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Women's issues were largely ignored and sex roles were reaffirmed; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Stalinism revived patriotic propaganda and Tsarist-era traditions, per Daniels.

gradual-change.rationale: Collectivization and industrialization were imposed rapidly from above.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The USSR was a closed state; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Stalin prized Soviet sovereignty and spoke of using force against aggressors; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Foreign trade was a state matter and Stalin described two rival world markets.

nation-first.rationale: Socialism in one country put the USSR's consolidation ahead of world revolution.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Intervention was justified in terms of security or class interest, not human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Borders and state are retained until capitalist encirclement ends; open borders are at best a distant aim.

limit-growth.rationale: Rapid industrial growth was the central aim of the Five-Year Plans (s1), so limiting growth is rejected, though no source addresses growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the productionist ideology puts growth first.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Stalinism pursued industrial and technical modernisation, while distorting some sciences.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from enthusiasm for heavy industry and state power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds revolution necessary; the USSR itself came from one.

experts-over-public.rationale: Stalin praised a new Soviet intelligentsia, while the party decided; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The planned economy replaced the NEP and Stalin defended its balanced-development law.

socialized-markets.rationale: Stalin kept commodity production in consumer goods, without private capital, for a period.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is state or collective property, so a land tax is moot; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Concentration of inherited wealth is contrary to socialism; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution is by work under socialism; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Foreign trade was controlled by the state to protect planned industry; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Investment followed the plan, with priority to heavy industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Collectivisation ended small peasant property (s5, s1), so a society of many small owners is rejected.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Stalin held that commodity circulation and money would vanish once a single sector replaced two, though wages remain under socialism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state bank is part of the planned economy; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wages and prices are set by the state plan; class struggle rather than partnership is the framework.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 126 of the 1936 Constitution names the Communist Party the vanguard of the working people and 'the leading core of all organizations of the working people, both public and state' (s7).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The regime was a revolutionary opponent of monarchy (s1). No source discusses monarchy's legitimacy directly.

democracy-best.rationale: The regime claimed to be democratic but ran a one-man police state and treated plain voter choice as bourgeois.

direct-votes.rationale: Real decisions rested with the party leadership; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviets were formally the organs of power but in practice were party-controlled.

right-to-secede.rationale: The formal doctrine of national self-determination included secession, but it was suppressed in practice.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leadership is justified by party doctrine and training, not by nature; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Great Terror executed hundreds of thousands (s1), and the doctrine of class struggle justified coercion, so a ban on all political violence is rejected. The statement is not discussed as a principle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Official rhetoric stressed peace and defence, not war as virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church and state were formally separated while religion was persecuted.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The state's militant atheism (s1) rules out scripture-based law, though the question is not discussed directly.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Stalin insisted on a strong state army and punitive organs (s2), which leaves no place for private courts or defence agencies. They are not discussed directly.

military-superiority.rationale: Stalin warned of capitalist encirclement and said the USSR would answer blow for blow.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The USSR was a multinational state built on the friendship of nations, though some peoples were deported.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle is the core of Marxism-Leninism, and Stalin held it to intensify.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism distributes by work; full equality comes only in communism; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Imperialism is condemned; reparations are inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Union was organised on class and ideological lines; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collectivist ethics reject individual self-interest as a moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual rights were subordinated to the party and the state (s1), so duties to the collective come first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The regime pursued the transformation of nature; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: The state encouraged births; abortion was banned in 1936.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrialisation was the central goal of the system (s1), so calling industrial civilisation a disaster is rejected. Not discussed directly.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Great Turn pushed rapid change regardless of disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; decisions rested with the party; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Stalin's view that a strong intelligence service is necessary (s2).

restore-past-order.rationale: The regime pursued progress toward communism, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy was justified by doctrine, such as the 1938 Short Course.

direct-action.rationale: Change was meant to come through the party and state, not spontaneous direct action; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Terror and coercion were used to build socialism (s1), so the means were not required to match the ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrialisation was the goal (s1), the opposite of a return to foraging, which no source discusses.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stalin said essential town-country and mental-manual distinctions will disappear, though some remain.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism is the stated eventual aim; socialism distributes by work.

production-for-use.rationale: Planned production for social needs is held to replace capitalist profit-seeking.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Stalin held that capitalist exploitation requires private ownership and wage labour, and denied it under socialism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Stalin described a first phase of the Soviet state as suppressing exploiting classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farms were the form of socialist agriculture; Stalin called the artel the main link.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Stalin held wars between capitalist countries remain inevitable while imperialism exists.

taxation-theft.rationale: State power and state extraction of the surplus were the basis of the system (s1), so taxation as theft is rejected. Not discussed directly.

harm-principle.rationale: The state controlled culture, speech and private life (s1), which rejects limiting state power to preventing harm. The principle is not discussed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The collective and the party come before individual rights (s1), which rejects a politics of individual rights alone.

conscription.rationale: Stalin held a large standing army essential amid capitalist encirclement (s2), which rests on universal military service. The 1939 report does not discuss conscription by name.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The regime restricted emigration and rejected exit as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a class and party instrument, not a firm; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material guarantees under the plan are stressed over negative liberty.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and universities were state-controlled instruments of the party.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Soviet doctrine was environmentalist, to the point of Lysenkoism.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation ran through the party and the soviets (s1), not through estates or corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: The state directed the economy, education and culture, including socialist realism.

national-rebirth.rationale: The aim was socialist construction, not national decadence and rebirth; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Soviet control extended over satellite states from 1944 to 1953.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on party and state, though loyalty to Stalin was demanded.

bound-labor.rationale: Stalin condemns extra-economic coercion as a feudal feature.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is understood as class-based; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Party doctrine claims to know the common interest; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The USSR backed Israel in 1948 but turned hostile to Zionism and 'cosmopolitans' soon after.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the closed-border, nationalities policy.

revive-national-language.rationale: Russification and Russian as de facto state language; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Enterprises were run through the plan and party; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from state control of education (s1); vouchers are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The question belongs to market economies; the planned economy has no such debate.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom is regarded as capitalist and replaced by planning.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from a system that rested on law, terror and an elaborate leader cult (s1).

national-self-determination.rationale: The formal nationalities doctrine upheld it, though it was overridden in practice.

force-without-un.rationale: Stalin said the USSR would respond with force to aggression; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dialectical materialism and atheism put scientific reason against religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the closed, state-centred system.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Distribution by work is the rule under socialism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rests on class struggle (s2), so collaboration between classes is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The regime used classical heritage and the Short Course; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Stalin described two hostile world camps and markets; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Socialism in one country gave national framing, though internationalism was professed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Formal law gave equality, though policy was pronatalist; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Private moneylending was incompatible with the planned economy; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Official doctrine proclaimed equality of races and friendship of nations.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Stalin described the state as an instrument to suppress exploiters and defend against encirclement.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic; a replacement conspiracy claim is alien to Marxism-Leninism, so the answer is inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Stalin dismissed the export of revolution as nonsense (s1), so a mission to spread the system abroad was played down.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Women's issues were largely ignored; class is the key analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Official doctrine treated bureaucrats as 'wreckers' to be purged, not the ruling party; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics was rejected in Soviet doctrine; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The NKVD operated as the state's instrument of terror, answerable to the leadership rather than to courts or the public (s1).

night-watchman-state.rationale: A strong, directing state is central to Stalin's doctrine (s2), the opposite of a minimal state, which is not discussed by name.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Official doctrine proclaimed friendship of nations and rejected racism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formal equality was proclaimed, though class enemies and ethnic groups were persecuted.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalin introduced the doctrine that socialism could be built in the USSR alone.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Marxism-Leninism condemns colonialism and imperialism; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Soviet law was uniform and secular; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No religious basis; collectivization led to mass livestock slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and enforced it in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin said the state will remain and be strengthened while capitalist encirclement lasts, and rebuked those who asked why it was not withering away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stalinism rested the party-state own right to rule on its vanguard role and the working class historic interest, not on the freely expressed agreement of the ruled, and it suppressed dissent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Stalinist doctrine treated science and culture as class-bound ('bourgeois' versus 'proletarian'), inferred from this Marxist-Leninist framing; Stalin also denied that language was class superstructure.

trade-surplus.rationale: The Soviet state monopolised foreign trade to import machinery and pursue self-sufficiency under encirclement; no stated doctrine on surpluses, so inferred and split.

population-transfer.rationale: Stalin's government deported whole nationalities it deemed disloyal, such as Chechens, Crimean Tatars and Volga Germans, as a security measure.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Stalinism justified forced collectivization and mass repression by the goal of socialism and an intensifying class struggle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Soviet doctrine credited planning and collective ownership, and promoted 'socialist emulation' rather than market rivalry; inferred from that economic model.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The one-party state suppressed all rival parties as agents of hostile classes and powers.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stalinism defined freedom through material security and the socialist state, and tolerated arbitrary party power; inferred, as the republican concept was not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet rule fused power in the party-state and rejected checks and balances as bourgeois forms.

vanguard-party.rationale: Stalinism inherited Lenin's doctrine of a disciplined vanguard party leading the working class and the state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The state claimed to rule for workers and peasants, but its policy priority was industrialization and state power; inferred from its class rhetoric.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing and land were state or collective property and the doctrine limited personal property to consumer goods, so a right to buy state homes fits poorly; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were effectively unlawful because unions were party-led bodies serving the plan; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxism-Leninism locates poverty in property relations and class rule, not in numbers of people, so the regime rejected the Malthusian view.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy officially preached internationalism and condemned national chauvinism, though it also deported peoples; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Office was filled by party appointment of cadres, and the regime treated plain voter choice as bourgeois; chance selection has no place.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Stalin argued that class struggle intensifies as socialism advances, and the regime justified mass repression and extrajudicial courts on that basis.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices and distribution were fixed by the state plan, and the state set prices under socialism.

party-controls-media.rationale: The press, radio and publishing were state and party controlled, with censorship to guide opinion.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stalin called for strengthening the army under party leadership, and political commissars made the army answer to the party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The USSR was a closed state that guarded entry and citizenship under encirclement; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Party maximum and the egalitarian rhetoric of Marxism-Leninism favoured modest official pay, though Stalin's regime in practice gave the elite large privileges and Stalin attacked wage equalisation; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism, with free debate then binding obedience, was the party rule Stalinism inherited and enforced to the extreme.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Stalin stressed the sovereign Soviet state under capitalist encirclement, and the regime treated the EU-style pooling of power as a capitalist arrangement; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive power was concentrated in Stalin and the party leadership, though formally the legislature was a rubber stamp; the statement's form is only loosely matched, so inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The regime persecuted the church, then in 1943 restored the bishop-led Moscow Patriarchate under state control; adherents had no view on church governance as such.

clerical-rule.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and persecuted clergy, so clerical authority over the state was unthinkable.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's revolutionary defeatism targeted capitalist powers, while Stalin demanded defence of the Soviet fatherland (s2, s4); adherents applied it to others' wars, not their own, so the application is split.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Socialist realism and state censorship shaped art to build the new Soviet person, as the Stalinist cultural system documents.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Stalin held office as General Secretary without term limits until death, and the one-party system had no limits on leaders; inferred for presidents.

recall-officials.rationale: Article 142 of the 1936 Constitution says a deputy 'is liable to be recalled at any time' by decision of a majority of the electors (s7), though the one-party system left it little used.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of socialism in one country and wary self-reliance toward capitalist powers; Stalin's postwar system however built alliances in the Soviet bloc.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing was state-owned and allocated under the planned economy rather than distributed as family-owned homes; no stated position on private ownership of homes.

people-in-arms.rationale: Stalinism built a large professional, party-controlled Red Army and treated military power as a state monopoly; inferred, not a stated position.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Stalin's works aim at removing the contrast between town and country and the programme was rapid urban industrialization; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: reunification was not a defined Stalinist principle and Soviet border policy was pragmatic.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Stalinism promoted a new Soviet intelligentsia and technical education, though intellectuals were also purged.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Soviet doctrine proclaimed equality of nations, yet Stalinism also ranked Russia first and class stages as higher; split, inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Stalinist rule used capital punishment extensively against alleged enemies of the state, as documented in the scholarship.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Stalin-era return to traditional family policy, including the 1936 abortion ban.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Stalinism presented itself as Marxism-Leninism, a materialist and atheist doctrine that rejected religious accounts of origins.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the state's control of culture and censorship under Stalinism, which restricted erotic material.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet approach to citizenship as tied to the state and class loyalty rather than ethnic descent; no stated position.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet nationalities policy of promoting national-language schools in the 1920s-30s, though it was later curtailed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from the Stalinist state's campaigns against religion, which allowed no exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the Stalinist demand for conformity and state control of personal life, art and thought.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Stalin's anti-imperialist line treats capitalist powers as exploiters of weaker countries, so writing off debts to them is inferred; no source addresses debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Stalin held that national freedom was tied to the socialist transformation of society; inferred from the 1939 report's account of the state and capitalist encirclement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The system rested on one-party rule and constitutions issued from the party leadership rather than freely elected assemblies; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid industrialization and forced collectivization were pursued under a one-party state that suppressed dissent in the name of building socialism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Stalin's writings frame foreign relations as a contest with capitalist encirclement rather than a universal duty of the rich to the poor; adherents are not clearly for or against.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Soviet security policy stressed self-reliance against capitalist encirclement, so an independent deterrent fits; nuclear weapons themselves are not discussed in the sources, so this is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Soviet head of state was chosen by the legislature under one-party control rather than by direct popular vote; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: All credit and finance were subordinated to the state plan, leaving no room for a bank independent of the government; inferred from the planning system.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Stalinism's sources do not address trading territory for peace and its record mixes annexation with diplomacy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Under Stalin's two property sectors, productive property is state or collective and subordinate to the plan, with personal property allowed; read as a common-good view, inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Stalin declared socialism built in the USSR and held that the state-owned planned economy was socialist, with exploitation abolished.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Stalinism put rapid industrial growth first, so restricting projects over uncertain risk cuts against it; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report favours mutual assistance pacts against aggressors, though Soviet practice was opportunistic; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The USSR annexed the Baltic states and eastern Poland in 1939-40 and treated them as legitimately incorporated; inferred from that practice.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Stalinism brought militant atheism and the persecution of religion, with church property taken and clergy placed under state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Party leader, identified with the state, was a partisan figure; the one-party state has no non-partisan head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 17 nominally allowed secession, but the regime crushed nationalist movements and deported peoples; practice favoured keeping territory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The republics were formally autonomous but all shared one socialist legal and economic system under Party direction.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Militant atheism rules out a sacred ruler; Stalin's cult was secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive tax on higher incomes fits socialist redistribution; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions form people, and the regime aimed to remake them, as in the 'new Soviet man'; Lysenkoism echoed this in biology.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Formally the state claimed socialist legality, but in practice Stalin and the Party stood above the law; adherents would not endorse the claim in doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Soviet space work was not a Stalin-era doctrinal goal and the question barely applies.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule is held to belong wholly to the working class through the Party's dictatorship of the proletariat, not a mix of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: From 1929 Stalin's image spread through statues, posters and banners and he was identified with the state.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family policy in this era (1944 law) favoured the state's interest in births and left fathers with few duties; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Stalin held that class struggle sharpens as socialism advances and justified purges by hidden enemies, including within the party.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land went to peasants in 1917, but Stalinism then collectivised it; only partly matches the statement, so inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The Stalinist state deported entire nationalities and did not honour return rights; inferred from practice.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Soviet expansion in 1939-40 used kin-people arguments in part but was framed by security and socialism; adherents give no clear doctrine.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church and state and equal rights for all; Stalinist practice persecuted religion but did not legislate against apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Stalinism was militantly secular and opposed religious dress and customs, so compelled covering is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Stalin kept national currencies and a closed monetary system under the plan; a shared currency is inferred as not a goal.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The USSR was built on a socialist union, not ethnic or kin unification across borders; Pan-Slavism was dismissed. Inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Soviet doctrine held nations should be national in form and socialist in content, run by a unified state; separate self-governing minority institutions are inferred as rejected.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Stalinist doctrine opposed Zionism and stressed assimilation within the Soviet state; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stalin held that economic laws and the mode of production determine social change, as in Marxist historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Stalinist economy is state-owned and planned, with concentration of production as policy; competition-based antitrust is inferred as rejected.

no-bailouts.rationale: State enterprises are propped up by the plan and not left to fail, so a ban on rescue is inferred as rejected.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: In the Stalinist state, courts and institutions answered to the party, so that majority and party will were not constrained; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights of women but set no representation quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from Stalin's socialism in one country amid capitalist encirclement (s2), which favoured economic independence; the statement's bloc wording is not discussed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Stalinism sought independence from capitalist markets, not binding standards imposed by trade deals; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Stalin held that socialism pays according to work, rejecting egalitarian levelling; moral incentives alone were not the doctrine, though used alongside.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Stalin favoured socialism in one country and rejected exporting revolution by small armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of origin and ended titles of the old order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Stalin-era socialism in one country was joined to Soviet patriotism and a nation-centred account of history; inferred from the overview, not from a specific source.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Stalinism condemned imperialism and colonial rule and the 1936 constitution proclaimed equal rights and a right of secession, so tutelage is rejected; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Soviet patriotism is a listed element of Stalinism, and schooling under Stalin was used to build loyalty to the Soviet state and its symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Korenizatsiia gave national preferences in the 1920s but was curtailed under Stalin, and the 1936 constitution proclaimed equal rights; Stalin's own works do not address it.

public-money-creation.rationale: A planned, state-owned economy leaves credit and money under state control; Stalin's works do not discuss money creation directly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Stalin held that capitalism is torn by contradictions, imperialist wars and a general crisis that make its eventual collapse inevitable.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Soviet policy sought lasting influence over neighbouring lands the Russian Empire had held, notably in Eastern Europe after 1945; inferred from Soviet practice.

delink-world-market.rationale: Stalin argued in 1952 that the world market had split into parallel socialist and capitalist markets and championed economic independence from the capitalist world; applied to poor countries by inference.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Stalin regarded the US working class as 'bourgeoisified' and played down advanced-country workers against Trotsky; the Wikipedia passage is itself marked citation needed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 1936 constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of nationality or race, and private enterprise was abolished, so private discrimination has no place.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1936 constitution listed rights but they were subordinate to the party and the plan, and it was amendable by the Supreme Soviet; limiting the state by entrenched rights runs against Stalinist theory.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Soviet policy treated border questions by its own interests (1939 pact, post-war frontiers); no clear stated principle, inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Soviet state rested on a one-party hierarchy, and heads of state were chosen by the party, not contested elections; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism subordinates minorities to the majority line, and dissent was repressed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The party-state treated resistance to the leadership as treason and counterrevolution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supreme Soviet was nominally the supreme body under the 1936 constitution but the party actually ruled; ambiguous.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Soviet life accepted animal welfare in principle; sources do not address it, so inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A utilitarian, productivist view accepts using animals for food and research; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity by the privileged is a class-society idea; socialism replaces it with state provision; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Citizens were expected to take part in building socialism and the Party; withdrawal was condemned.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist theory fits the claim but Stalinist culture used mass media to mobilise its own order; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxism-Leninism accepts that bourgeois rule works partly through ideology and culture, in addition to force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Stalin's account of imperialism holds that capitalist states exploit colonies and weaker countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Soviet Union formally promoted equality among nationalities; reserving offices by birth is contrary to its stated line, though inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Stalinism demanded the Comintern follow Moscow's direction; foreign parties were subordinated to the CPSU.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Socialism in one country: the USSR built industry on its own resources and under capitalist encirclement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Soviet territorial policy recovered lands lost to Tsarist Russia in 1939-45, but no general principle is stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Soviet policy was class-based and promoted all nationalities as equal; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Antifascism was central to Stalinist legitimacy, especially after 1941, and to Soviet foreign policy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Stalinism treated fascism as the open terrorist dictatorship of finance capital and communism as its opposite.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Soviet historiography held that the Civil War was fought over slavery and the Southern slaveholders' rebellion; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Soviet practice destroyed monuments of the old regime; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Soviet ideology held that sex equality is achieved by socialism and had no men's programmes; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Soviet ideology treated domestic violence as a vestige of the old order, not as gendered symmetry; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims universal validity and had no pluralism of political forms; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party controls the army, which is subordinate to it, with political commissars; the army may not act independently.

paid-care-work.rationale: Stalinism socialised domestic labour through services but did not endorse paying household work; mixed and inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Soviet family policy of the 1930s restored parental authority and strengthened the family, though lifelong support of parents is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Soviet system selected officials through party nomenclature and promoted cadres by party loyalty and training, not by examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The state held a monopoly on foreign trade and owned all strategic industry, so foreign takeover of firms was impossible.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The 1936 family policy of the Stalin era made divorce harder, with fees and court procedure, and banned abortion.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Article 142 (s7) makes deputies recallable at any time by their electors, but nothing provides for binding instructions, so the delegate model is only partly met.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Stalinism ran a state-owned economy with state social insurance, so private pension accounts were incompatible.

land-use-tenure.rationale: All land was nationalised in the USSR and collective farms held it in perpetual use, which matches holding land by use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Supreme Soviet formally approved the budget, but real control lay with the party, so adherents saw approval as a formality rather than a check.

single-official-language.rationale: Russian was promoted as the common language of the Soviet state and schooling in the late Stalin years, though the constitution formally gave republics their own languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land was nationalised and no foreigner could own it under the Soviet system.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Stalinist doctrine defined discrimination by class and intent under the 1936 constitution's equality of rights, not by outcome statistics.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Stalinist ideology's critique of capitalist consumption, though Stalin also promoted a 'cultured' prosperity in the 1930s.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Soviet Union under Stalin backed communist parties and insurgents abroad through the Comintern and later in Greece and Korea.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Stalin imposed Soviet-aligned systems on Eastern Europe and pressured Tito's Yugoslavia after the 1948 break (s1), but there was no invasion of an ally, so the answer is inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that the state under capitalism serves the capitalist class, so corporate sway over government is read as class rule.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report treats the USSR as besieged by capitalist encirclement and hostile foreign agents, which supports state control of foreign-funded media and organisations.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Stalin-era family policy, including the 1936 abortion ban and 1944 awards for large families, aimed to raise births through state incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land and housing were state-controlled and decisions came from the central plan, not local authorities; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1936 constitution guarantees the right to work and the planned economy was meant to provide employment for all.

democratic-peace.rationale: Stalin held that wars between capitalist states and imperialist wars are inevitable and presented liberal democracy as bourgeois dictatorship, rejecting the democratic-peace claim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Stalinist state demanded unconditional obedience and treated disobedience as sabotage, and Stalin held that the state endures under socialism.

non-intervention.rationale: Stalinism backed proletarian internationalism and Soviet intervention abroad, though Stalin publicly stressed non-interference; inferred and mixed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet trade unions were organised by industry under party leadership; inferred from the structure and not from the cited sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Stalin-era campaigns against 'rootless cosmopolitans', the Doctors' Plot and deported nationalities treated minorities as hostile to the Soviet state; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Stalin reversed the early Soviet liberalisation of family law and strengthened registered marriage as a state institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Stalinist state ran censorship and secrecy and treated information as a state monopoly.

local-production.rationale: Stalinism built a nationally planned division of labour and heavy industry rather than local self-sufficiency; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Democratic centralism and the party's monopoly make autonomous informal groups illegitimate and subject to repression.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Socialism in one country and capitalist encirclement lead to a stress on Soviet sovereignty over outside legal authority.

religious-nation.rationale: The Soviet state was officially atheist and the 1936 constitution separates church and state, so the nation is not defined by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Stalin spoke of equal peaceful relations between states and defended Soviet sovereignty, and no source calls for tribute; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A centrally planned economy under one plan pools resources by state decision rather than leaving regions to keep their revenue; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 10 of the 1936 Constitution protects personal ownership of income, savings, homes and articles of personal use while the means of production are socialist property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Stalinism is itself the communist system and treated capitalist encirclement as hostile, so it seeks capitalism overthrown, not communism defeated.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: State and collective ownership of services and industry was the rule, with no place for private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats religion as a product of old social conditions that withers under socialism, though the Soviet state combined this with repression and wartime concessions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds capitalism was progressive against feudalism by building productive forces; inferred from the orthodox doctrine rather than Stalin-specific texts.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Soviet doctrine tied women's emancipation to socialist economic transformation (Article 122 equal rights), though Stalin declared the question largely solved; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Stalinist family policy of the 1930s-40s promoted the family and restricted divorce and abortion, rejecting early Bolshevik plans for socialised housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: No Stalinist programme of purging loanwords is documented and Soviet policy kept internationalist vocabulary; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Stalinism centralised power over national republics despite the formal right of secession, and overrode arrangements by force, including deportations; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Collective farms (artels) were set up under state direction within a centralised state, not as independent self-governing communities replacing it.

majority-settlement.rationale: Soviet policy encouraged Russian settlement in non-Russian republics and deported minorities; inferred as agreement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Stalinism is a form of communism and presents it as the sound basis for society.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Stalinism's Marxism-Leninism rested on class, not ancestral right, though Stalin's state used national claims in practice; inferred from its internationalist doctrine.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Soviet state documented and prosecuted Nazi mass murder, including at Nuremberg, so denial of the established account is rejected, though the Soviet record presented victims as Soviet citizens.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Stalinist state recriminalised male homosexuality in 1934 and treated it as a bourgeois vice.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The one-party state, the secret police and the Great Purge justified suppression of opponents as an intensifying class struggle.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Stalinism was officially atheist and persecuted churches, but it did not punish blasphemy as an offence against a state religion; it suppressed religion rather than defended any.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats colonialism as imperialist exploitation to be ended; the 1939 report and Stalin's other works attack capitalist imperialism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The Soviet state opposed religious mobilisation, though it backed anti-colonial resistance; the statement's religious duty is inferred to be rejected.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Stalinism was officially atheist and the state rested on party rule, not religious law, so it rejects religious legitimacy tests and suppressed armed religious movements.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The 1936 Constitution framed Soviet democracy through soviets and the party, while Stalinism rejected independent initiative from below as a threat; participation was directed from the centre.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Stalinism held that class struggle is the basic cleavage and that the 1936 Constitution had abolished exploitation; separate or overlapping oppressions were treated as secondary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Stalinist state criminalised homosexuality and promoted the traditional family in the 1930s; legal recognition of gender identity would be rejected.

assisted-dying.rationale: Stalinism did not address assisted dying; a state that stressed population and labour power is inferred to disagree.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Stalinism held that politics is class struggle between socialism and capitalism, and treated claims of a third way as capitalist or social-fascist deviations.

alienated-labor.rationale: Stalinism held that capitalist labour exploits workers and that exploitation ended under socialism (s6); the Marxist concept of alienation itself was little used, so this is inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Stalinism opposed all religions as backward but did not hold a cultural claim about Islam and the West; this is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stalinism was officially atheist and grounded authority in the working class as led by the party; the 1936 Constitution says power belongs to the working people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Soviet state was officially atheist and kept religion out of state institutions and schools, so a ban on religious dress there fits its policy.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Stalinism had no position on nondisclosure agreements; the state owned the economy and the issue did not arise.

social-market-economy.rationale: Stalinism built a planned state-owned economy and treated commodity production under socialism as a limited survival; it rejected both market and mixed models.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Stalin argued that wars among capitalist states are inevitable and that the Soviet Union must be strongly armed; abolishing armed forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Stalinism pursued rapid, planned industrialization of the whole country, and the 1936 Constitution presents socialism as ending class inequality; letting some grow rich first is rejected, though planners favoured heavy industry over consumers.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Stalin's USSR led the socialist camp and opposed the capitalist bloc, though it signed the 1939 pact with Germany for tactical reasons; permanent neutrality was not its doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Stalin ruled a Marxist-Leninist republic whose 1936 constitution provides for elected soviets; hereditary succession of the leader was not its practice or doctrine, though the cult of personality was strong.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Stalinism put all credit in state banks under central planning, so private or mutual user-owned banks lay outside its system.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Stalinism stressed building socialism in one country with economic independence from capitalist states, so lender-imposed conditions would be rejected; inferred from this.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave universal and equal suffrage to all citizens and abolished the property and class disqualifications that the earlier constitution had imposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Stalinism subordinated nature to industrialization while its constitution proclaimed women equal to men; the ecofeminist linkage is not part of it.

reification.rationale: Stalinist Marxism-Leninism accepted the critique of commodity fetishism in principle, yet Stalin held that commodity production persists under socialism and the term was not central; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed press and assembly by placing printing presses and halls at the disposal of workers, on the premise that the bourgeoisie had controlled them.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Stalinism ruled by party decree and mass repression justified by class struggle, though it proclaimed a constitution and courts; the statement as written is not its practice.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1936 Constitution proclaimed equal rights for citizens regardless of nationality or race and made any racial privilege a punishable offence.

online-participation.rationale: Stalinism predates the internet and its centralised, party-led model gives no stated view; adherents would differ.

open-government-data.rationale: Stalinism kept state records and decisions under party secrecy; inferred from its practice of secrecy and control.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Stalinism was officially atheist and hostile to religion, but its 1936 Constitution proclaimed equal rights regardless of religion; restricting interfaith marriage is inferred to be disfavoured.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Stalinism officially opposed religious and national discrimination, and the 1936 Constitution made equal rights regardless of nationality or creed a principle.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Stalinist rule vested decisions in the party and state organs, not citizens chosen by lot; the 1936 constitution provides for elected soviets only.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Stalinism treated religion as a survival to be curbed, not something to reform; the statement's implied support for religious modernisation is not its position, though the wartime church concordat shows tactical use of religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Stalinism ended private ownership of the means of production to stop exploitation by owners of capital; the claim that concentrated wealth threatens freedom is inferred from that, though the system itself concentrated power in the state.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Soviet state recriminalised male homosexuality in 1934 and treated it as a bourgeois vice, so open service would have been rejected.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Stalinist state ran anti-religious education and propaganda, under a Marxist-Leninist view of religion as a survival of the old order, though it eased the campaign during the war.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Stalin held that the state, with its army, police and security organs, must grow stronger under capitalist encirclement rather than wither away, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The 1936 Constitution made the USSR a federation of republics under one party; power-sharing among communities as a way of limiting the centre is inferred to be rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees care and support through state social insurance and state-run services, so the state, not charity, is meant to provide for the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Stalin held office as General Secretary for decades with no limit, and the Constitution sets none for the party leadership; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Democratic centralism and a single party left no room for revocable delegation of votes by policy area; inferred from the system's structure.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The doctrine never addressed human extinction and put priority on industrial, military and class goals; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religion was suppressed, so the question hardly arises, but the Constitution (art. 122) gave women equal rights in all spheres; inferred that adherents would not bar them.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Article 122 of the 1936 Constitution declares women equal to men in all spheres of life, which implies shared rather than husband-held authority in the household.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution reserved voting to Soviet citizens, and the system was suspicious of foreigners and foreign influence.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: the planned, state-owned economy set prices and housing allocation by administrative decision rather than the market.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: Stalin-era theory treated ownership of the means of production as a social matter, but it kept author rights and inventors' rewards, so abolition was not a stated aim.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet state organised youth in the Pioneers and Komsomol under Party direction, though the sources used here do not discuss them.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: the USSR built its own nuclear arsenal in 1949 and treated military strength as vital under capitalist encirclement.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet state treated foreign military presence as a threat from capitalist encirclement and hosted no Western bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the regime itself deported whole peoples and denied or concealed its own mass killings, and adherents would not accept formal recognition as a duty.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution states the socialist principle 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his work' and bars income from ownership of means of production.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The ideology glorified the defence of the socialist fatherland and mass repression justified by class struggle, so a ban on killing in self-defence is foreign to it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: Stalin-era rule revived Russian patriotic history to build loyalty, though it did not frame national identity as unbroken from ancient origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist materialism, which treated sex as biological; later Soviet policy defined gender roles through the family and the state.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Stalinism treated class, not gender, as the basis of politics, and the Soviet state defined women as a single category of workers and mothers.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the regime honoured those who died for the Soviet cause as heroes, though it was atheist and did not speak of saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Stalinism rested on dialectical materialism, which understood politics as class struggle, not as a spiritual contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: Soviet policy treated diaspora nationalism with suspicion and favoured territorial national units within the USSR.

culture-before-state.rationale: Stalinism put the state first, building the state and its industry before any cultural renewal; the culture was to serve the Party's aims.

god-not-male.rationale: The atheist ideology had no stance on how God is described, which it treated as irrelevant.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The ideology rejected religious texts as such, so judging them by this test is not at issue.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: Soviet nationality policy officially rejected favouring one national majority, though late Stalinism favoured Russians.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: Soviet policy organised republics and autonomous regions along national lines, giving each nation its own territorial unit.

independent-unions.rationale: Under Stalinism the unions were transmission belts of the Party and state, not independent bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Stalin presented the USSR as a socialist state of workers and peasants led by the Party, so adherents hold that the working class rules through it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public utilities and services sat inside the state-owned sector of the planned economy.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1936 Constitution created a Supreme Soviet with two chambers, the Soviet of the Union and the Soviet of Nationalities.

municipal-property.rationale: Socialist property was either state property or the collective-farm sector; municipal ownership as a separate third form was not a Stalinist category.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism put decisions in the central Party and state, not in local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Stalin-era pro-natalist and family-strengthening policy described in the overview, not from a stated wage doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: no source states a view; the Soviet state prized medical science but also controlled it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: no source states a view on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from a state monopoly on money and a planned economy that left no room for untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the surveillance and political policing that characterised Stalinist rule.

person-over-state.rationale: Stalinist rule subordinated individuals to the state and Party, with mass repression of those seen as obstacles.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The regime was officially atheist and materialist and persecuted religion, though the 1936 Constitution separated church and state.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The 1936 Constitution formally granted a right of secession, but the Union was in practice centralised; inferred that adherents accept formal revocable autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the push for large-scale mechanised agriculture and technological modernisation.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: Stalinism urbanised rapidly and sought to abolish town and country differences, but took no stated view on density and the environment.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Stalinism held that class, not race, defined political interests, and the 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from official internationalism and equal-rights doctrine, though Russian national pride was promoted in the 1930s and 1940s.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Stalin held wars among capitalist states to be inevitable and the USSR pursued territorial expansion in 1939-1945; adherents nonetheless call Soviet policy a peace policy.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Stalin defined a nation by common language, territory, economy and culture, but the regime subordinated language-based claims across borders to Soviet state interests; a mild disagree with the cross-border form.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave equal rights regardless of religion or nationality, and one-party rule left no room for religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Stalin's works cast capitalist encirclement as hostile and the show trials presented foreign powers as plotting against the USSR.

free-public-college.rationale: Article 121 of the 1936 Constitution makes education, including higher education, free of charge (s7), but Stalin's government introduced tuition fees for higher education in 1940, so doctrine and practice diverge.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution taxes are a market instrument; Stalinist planning relied on directives and ignored environmental costs; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Rhetoric looked to a future communist society, but practice sacrificed the environment to industrialization; adherents are not clearly for or against.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Stalinism treated women's equality as equal participation in labour and party life, not as distinct values to be weighted more; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Stalin held war between states inevitable while capitalism lasted and built up massive armaments, so reducing them to a minimum is rejected.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Stalin's diplomacy included the secret protocols of the 1939 pact with Germany, and the regime ran on secrecy.

capital-controls.rationale: A planned economy with a state monopoly of foreign trade means the state controls capital movement across the border.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Stalinist state held a monopoly of armed force through the army and NKVD and suppressed all independent armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Red Army demanded unconditional obedience, and refusal of orders was punished as treason; wars were framed as defence of the socialist state.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Soviet trade unions were transmission belts of the Party and wages were set by state planning, not by bargaining with employers.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: wages and social benefits were fixed by the state plan, so a tax-credit top-up is not part of the model.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: a planned economy financed by state credit and the budget has no use for legally binding borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from Stalin's analysis of imperialism and capitalist encirclement; the USSR backed anti-colonial and anti-capitalist forces, though less for developing-country fairness than for socialism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Stalin kept the Leninist view that the bourgeois state was smashed in 1917 and replaced by Soviets, while holding that the new state must then be strengthened.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Stalin insisted on a single state-planned socialist economy and treated commodity production as a limited survival to be superseded.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: planning treated natural resources as state property to be used for production, not priced as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from the 1930s turn to Soviet patriotism and Russian national tradition; it was not a sacred-nation doctrine.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution guaranteed free education including higher education, so there were no student loans to cancel.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Official doctrine held that the USSR had abolished exploitation among its nations, so a core exploiting its regions was denied.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: Stalinism aimed to remould people into new Soviet citizens and treated human nature as shaped by social conditions.

public-service-media.rationale: All press and broadcasting were owned and directed by the Party-state, and independence from government was not tolerated.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marxism-Leninism under Stalin was officially atheist and treated religion as false consciousness, with anti-religious campaigns, so no religion was held to express a true spiritual reality.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the state purchase of crops and the collective-farm (artel) system, which replaced the market; the aim was extraction for industrialization more than farmer security.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from capitalist encirclement and the Soviet bomb of 1949; the USSR proposed bans but did not disarm unilaterally while rivals held weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Communist Party was presented as the party of the working class, the vanguard that represents workers separately from other classes' parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet campaign against harmful customary practices and the state's secular, modernizing law; the issue itself was not addressed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees women equal rights with men in all spheres of economic and public life, and Soviet law gave equal inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from Soviet nationality policy, which codified distinct national languages for each republic and nationality (1936 Constitution's republics) rather than merging them.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A state-owned planned economy handles harm through plans, ministries and administrative rules, with no independent private suits against state enterprises.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Stalinism fought traditional and customary elites (clergy, kulaks, local notables) and vested all lawmaking in the Soviets and the Party.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Rapid industrialization took precedence over conservation, but liberty was also not valued, so this is a mild rejection of the environment-first framing.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from harsh codified penalties and decrees that set heavy fixed punishments, plus extrajudicial bodies that left little judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the 1930s Russian-language policy; the Soviet state promoted Russian as the common language, and immigration was barely an issue.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Soviet trade unions were state-run organs under the Party, and membership was effectively expected; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Soviet elections had a single list, so voter identification was not a live issue; inferred as neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church and state and guarantees equal rights, though in practice religion was repressed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Stalinism rejected competitive multiparty elections and claimed democracy meant socialist substance under Party rule.

premarital-sex.rationale: Stalin-era family policy was socially conservative, with the 1936 abortion ban and promotion of the stable family.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: A state that controlled communications and the press would accept cutting access in a crisis; anachronistic inference.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A state-planned economy with state and collective sectors would not replace welfare programs with a market-style cash payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave women equal rights with men in political life, including voting and office.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats religion as a backward institution and Soviet policy campaigned against it; inferred for women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Official Soviet doctrine condemned racism and the Soviet system claimed equal rights of nationalities; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Party's women's department was abolished in 1930 on the claim the women's question was solved; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Stalinist doctrine holds that land and natural resources are state property and that private appropriation of them is abolished; the two socialist sectors are state and collective-farm property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The USSR took part in prosecuting Axis leaders but rejected any authority over its own conduct, so a committed Stalinist would be split; inferred from this, not stated in the sources.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Stalinism is built on Marxism-Leninism, which treats religion as ideology and a competitor to the party, and the state conducted anti-religious campaigns.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the 1936 constitution's guarantee of women's equal rights, and from the Soviet claim to have liberated women; it is not stated for group self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defence of the USSR as the socialist state against capitalist encirclement was central to Stalin's doctrine; Stalinists deny that the bureaucracy changes its class character, so they would agree strongly.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the 1936 constitution, which introduced direct elections to the soviets in place of the earlier tiered system; real selection stayed party-controlled.

national-church-status.rationale: The 1936 constitution separates church from state and school, and Stalinist policy gave no church a privileged status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy gave union and autonomous republics and regions to national groups, 'national in form, socialist in content', though under central party control.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Stalinist practice settled territorial questions by state interest and class considerations, with plebiscites used only as formal endorsement.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The USSR kept most imperial Russian borders internally while backing anti-colonial movements; no doctrine on this is stated.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Stalinist stress on industrial growth and rising material welfare as the aim of socialism, as in the 1952 text.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Soviet policy, which encouraged migration of Russians and others into national regions rather than limiting it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: Soviet universal conscription of the period applied to men, with women serving only as volunteers; the sources do not address it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Stalinism was internationalist and anti-religious in doctrine, but wartime Soviet patriotism stressed defending the motherland; inferred and split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Soviet practice used mass shootings without trial, though the doctrine presented them as legal; the statement targets drug users, so the answer is inferred from the regime's use of terror.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Soviet Union under Stalin had no relations with China as a partner on that footing; inferred as outside the period, and the question is anachronistic.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The 1936 constitution and Stalin's report stress the Soviet state, not kin abroad; deportations of minorities contradicted any such protection; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Stalinist doctrine held the land and natural resources as state property of the whole people, though it gave no right to compensation.

self-ownership.rationale: Stalinism subordinated the individual to the state and the plan, and used forced labour and collectivization, so it rejects full individual rights over one's body and labour.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The Soviet state relied on turnover taxes on consumer goods as a main source of revenue; inferred from practice, so cutting them is against it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Stalinism favoured universal state provision of health and education as a socialist principle, not poverty targeting; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Party and mass organisations were the channel of rule under Stalin, and the Party stood between the leader and the people; bypassing it contradicts the doctrine.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Socialism abolished private business altogether, so there was no scope for private privileges; inferred as agreement in principle.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1936 constitution separated church from state, and the regime suppressed religious organisation of any kind.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Stalinism pursued rapid industrialisation and modernisation and rejected appeals to the traditions of the past; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The 1936 constitution gave women equal rights, and Soviet law allowed divorce on request; the later 1944 restrictions complicate this.

national-resource-control.rationale: Socialism meant state ownership of resources and the Soviet Union was ruled against foreign capital under capitalist encirclement.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Stalinism judged justice by class outcomes and abolished private ownership of the means of production, so a procedure-based test of just distribution contradicts it; inferred from its collectivist principles.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; a state-planned economy with a closed financial system has no use for global currency markets, so a tax on them is inferred as unwelcome or irrelevant.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Stalinism claimed racial and national oppression ended with the 1936 constitution's equality, but the question concerns disadvantaged groups in other societies and is not addressed; adherents give no clear answer.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: the Stalinist state treated law as an instrument of party and class power, and its repression ran through formally lawful courts and decrees, so higher-law claims are rejected.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Stalin's writings stress abolishing the gap between mental and physical labour and raising workers' culture, but no shorter-week automation goal is stated; the answer is inferred and ambiguous.

multipolar-world.rationale: Stalin argued capitalist states would fight each other and the USSR stood against encirclement, which fits multipolar thinking, but Stalinism also sought Soviet-led socialist camp primacy; adherents are split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Stalin's Economic Problems of the USSR keeps the law of value operating only within limits under socialism, and the Marxism-Leninism it claimed holds labour as the source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Stalinism after the 1930s promoted Soviet patriotism and the defence of the fatherland as the cause of the working people, as in the 1939 report and the Great Patriotic War propaganda.

material-over-identity.rationale: Stalinism defined itself by class and material interests of workers, though the question is about the left in capitalist countries and is inferred from that class focus.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Stalin allowed commodity production and money to persist within a state-owned planned economy under party leadership, but rejected a genuine market economy; the answer is a partial disagreement.

missingStatements.text: A socialist state should grow stronger, not wither away, for as long as it is surrounded by hostile states.
missingStatements.rationale: Stalin argued explicitly that the state persists and strengthens under capitalist encirclement and criticised Party members who asked why it was not dying out.

notes: Stalinism is contested as a category: its adherents regard it as simply Marxism-Leninism, and historians disagree over its continuity with Lenin. Practice (terror, deportations) often diverged from the formal doctrine, so answers on equality and self-determination are low confidence.
